headline: Teargas fired as garment workers clash with police in Mirpur
summary: Protests over minimum wage demands enter their fourth day, with clashes in Mirpur-11 and reports of 200 factories closing in Savar and Ashulia.
details: Garment workers in Mirpur-11 clashed with police today after attempting to take to the streets to demand a higher minimum wage. Law enforcement officers used teargas shells and sound grenades to disperse the crowds.

The unrest began after workers walked out of several factories around 10:00 am. By 10:30 am, they gathered in alleys and attempted to reach the main road, leading to a chased and counter-chase scenario with police for nearly half an hour.
During the clash, workers reportedly hurled brickbats at police. Police responded by firing teargas and sound grenades, forcing the workers to retreat from the main road and nearby alleys.

Following the dispersal, members of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the main road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage by infiltrated Awami League members.
Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the DMP's Public Order Management division, stated that 'miscreants with ulterior motives' were involved in the movement, rather than actual workers.
The protests over minimum wage demands have now entered their fourth consecutive day, with reports of 200 factories closing in Savar and Ashulia due to the suis unrest.
Additionally, workers in Savar and Narayanganj have blocked highways, further escalating the tensions in the industrial belts.
caption:

During the clash, workers reportedly hurled brickbats at police. Police responded by firing teargas and sound grenades, forcing the workers to retreat from the main road and nearby alleys.

Following the dispersal, members of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal and Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal took positions on the main road, claiming they were there to prevent sabotage by infiltrated Awami League members.

Touhidul Arif, deputy commissioner of the DMP's Public Order Management division, stated that 'miscreants with ulterior motives' were involved in the movement, rather than actual workers.

The protests over minimum wage demands have now entered their fourth consecutive day, with reports of 200 factories closing in Savar and Ashulia due to the suis unrest.

Additionally, workers in Savar and Narayanganj have blocked highways, further escalating the tensions in the industrial belts.

headline_marked: 16 held as [[garment workers protest for Tk 30,000 wage]] in Mirpur
headline: 16 held as garment workers protest for Tk 30,000 wage in Mirpur
summary: Police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters beneath the Mirpur-11 metro rail station during the sixth day of unrest.
details: Police arrested 16 people in Mirpur on Tuesday, marking the sixth day of protests by garment workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.
On Tuesday morning, police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters gathered beneath the Mirpur-11 metro rail station.
In a separate incident on Kalshi Road, a police officer was reportedly surrounded and beaten by protesters.
The unrest has spread to Gazipur and Savar, where workers have been demonstrating for higher wages and clashing with law enforcement.
Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed in Gazipur, Narayanganj, and nearby industrial areas to maintain order.
Authorities have announced plans to strengthen surveillance using drones and body-worn cameras to monitor the situation.
caption:
16 arrested in Mirpur as garment workers clash with police over a Tk 30,000 minimum wage demand.

Police arrested 16 people in Mirpur on Tuesday, marking the sixth day of protests by garment workers demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk 30,000.

On Tuesday morning, police used tear gas and sound grenades to disperse protesters gathered beneath the Mirpur-11 metro rail station.

In a separate incident on Kalshi Road, a police officer was reportedly surrounded and beaten by protesters.

The unrest has spread to Gazipur and Savar, where workers have been demonstrating for higher wages and clashing with law enforcement.

Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel have been deployed in Gazipur, Narayanganj, and nearby industrial areas to maintain order.

Authorities have announced plans to strengthen surveillance using drones and body-worn cameras to monitor the situation.
